title: Substitute and global
summary: Search and replace across a file with :s and :%s, and run commands on matching lines with :g.

steps.title: :s and :%s
body: :s/old/new/          first match on the current line
:s/old/new/g         every match on the current line
:%s/old/new/g        every match in the whole file  (% = all lines)
:'<,'>s/old/new/g    only the visual selection (vim fills in '<,'> when you press : in visual mode)

The search part is a regex. In the replacement, `&` is the whole match and `\1` a captured group: `:%s/\(\w\+\)=\(\w\+\)/\2=\1/` swaps `key=value`. Any delimiter works, which helps with paths: `:%s#/usr/local#/opt#g`.
> **Practise:** open **Labs → Vim & nano trainer** and run this lesson's challenges until the keys come without thinking.

steps.prompt: Match the command to what it replaces.
pairs: the first `a` on the current line
every `a` in the file, confirming each

steps.prompt: The file has these lines. You run `:%s/80/8080/` (no `g`). What is the file now?
steps.explain: Without `g`, only the **first** match on each line is replaced, but `%` still visits every line.

steps.prompt: Replace every `/var/www` path with `/srv/www` in the whole file, without escaping the slashes.
steps.explain: Using `#` as the delimiter avoids writing `\/` for every slash.

steps.title: :g, the global command
body: `:g/pattern/command` runs an Ex command on every line that matches; `:v/pattern/command` (or `:g!`) on every line that does **not**.
:g/TODO/s/TODO/DONE/   substitute only on lines with TODO
:g/pattern/m0       move matching lines to the top (reverses their order!)

steps.explain: `^#` means the line **starts** with `#`. An indented comment starts with spaces, so it survives (use `^\s*#` to catch it).

steps.prompt: What does `:v/ERROR/d` do to a log file?
options: Deletes every line that does **not** contain ERROR, leaving only errors
Shows ERROR lines without changing anything

steps.title: A :s engine
prompt: Write `List<string> Substitute(List<string> lines, int current, string command)` that runs a substitute command. `current` is the cursor line (0-based). The command has the form `<range>s<d><pattern><d><replacement><d><flags>` where:
- `<range>` is empty (current line only), `%` (all lines) or `a,b` (1-based, inclusive),
- `<d>` is the delimiter: whatever character follows the `s`,
- `<pattern>` is a **plain string** (not a regex here), `<replacement>` is plain text,
- `<flags>` may contain `g` (all matches on a line, otherwise only the first) and `i` (ignore case).
Matches do not overlap. The command starts with `:`. Return the new lines.
starter: List<string> Substitute(List<string> lines, int current, string command)
solution: List<string> Substitute(List<string> lines, int current, string command)
string pattern = parts[0], replacement = parts.Length > 1 ? parts[1] : "", flags = parts.Length > 2 ? parts[2] : "";
for (int r = from; r <= to && r < result.Count; r++)
int at = pattern.Length == 0 ? -1 : line.IndexOf(pattern, i, cmp);
if (at < 0) { sb.Append(line, i, line.Length - i); break; }
if (!global) { sb.Append(line, i, line.Length - i); break; }
hints: Find the `s`, then the delimiter is the next character; `Split(d)` gives pattern, replacement and flags.
Replace in a loop with `IndexOf(pattern, i, comparison)`, stopping after one unless `g`.
template: Dojo.Eq("current line, first match", new List<string> { "listen 8080; # 80", "port=80", "Port=80" }, Substitute(dojoF, 0, ":s/80/8080/"));
Dojo.Eq("current line, g", new List<string> { "listen 8080; # 8080", "port=80", "Port=80" }, Substitute(dojoF, 0, ":s/80/8080/g"));
Dojo.Eq("range 2,3 with i", new List<string> { "listen 80; # 80", "PORT=80", "PORT=80" }, Substitute(dojoF, 0, ":2,3s/port/PORT/i"));
Dojo.Eq("case-sensitive by default", new List<string> { "listen 80; # 80", "PORT=80", "Port=80" }, Substitute(dojoF, 0, ":%s/port/PORT/g"));
Dojo.Eq("another delimiter", new List<string> { "root /srv/www;" }, Substitute(new List<string> { "root /var/www;" }, 0, ":s#/var/www#/srv/www#"));
